en: Slide Ch.2 p.25 (image viewed): the η_Otto(r) curve ends at ≈ 0.665 at r = 14; the k = 1.4 formula gives 0.652. The 0.013 gap is inside the reading error (±0.02): not an error, only a graph that does not follow k = 1.4 exactly everywhere.

Slide Ch.2 p.30 (image viewed): the Diesel efficiency formula carries the label "η th,Otto" (it should read th,Diesel). The content 1 − (T₄−T₁)/[k(T₃−T₂)] is right; verify_m02.py checks it with the 1→4 temperature chain.

Slide Ch.2 p.40 (image viewed): the η_Brayton(r_p) curve lies above the k = 1.4 formula at large r_p: the figure reads ≈ 0.63 at r_p = 20 (formula 0.575) and ≈ 0.653 at r_p = 25 (0.601); the slide caption states neither k nor the specific-heat assumption. The formula on p.39 stays correct; do not use this graph to check a cold-air calculation.

Slide Ch.2 p.40: r_p = 8.2 for maximum work is exact only for constant k (the formula gives 8.223). With variable specific heats verify_m02.py measures ≈ 9.13 (A-2c polynomial) and 9.08 (CoolProp); w_net(8.2)/w_max = 0.998 so the maximum is very flat. Linear interpolation of Table A-17 makes the w_net(r_p) curve bumpy (±0.5 kJ/kg) so the location of the maximum is unstable (points within 0.3 kJ/kg of the maximum span 8.85–9.30). The "≈ 8.0 from A-17" noted earlier in the project is this interpolation noise, not a reliable number: recorded for awareness, the slide is not changed.
Slide Ch.2 p.44 (image viewed): the denominator of ε reads "q regen,mã"; it means q_regen,max.

Slide Ch.2 p.45 (image viewed): the "with regeneration" curves of the figure correspond to T₁/T₃ = 0.2, 0.25, 0.33 and change from solid to dashed after the crossing with the no-regeneration curve; the k = 1.4 formula puts the crossing at r_p = (T₃/T₁)^(k/[2(k−1)]) (verify_m02.py checks it with sympy: x² = T₃/T₁).

Slide Ch.2 pp.46–48 (image of p.48 viewed): the title is truncated in the text extraction; the image shows the full "The Brayton cycle with intercooling, reheating, and regeneration", i.e. reheating and regeneration are included (10 states).

Slide Ch.2 p.52 (image viewed) and Cengel §9-11: "propulsive efficiency" η_P = Ẇ_p/Q̇_in (thrust power over heat added). This is the OVERALL efficiency η_o of Farokhi (Eq. 4.85–4.88 define the propulsive efficiency as F·V₀/ΔK̇E ≈ 2V₀/(V₉ + V₀)) and El-Sayed. One name, two different quantities: the m02 questions use the slide's definition and say so.
Slide Ch.2 p.19: "four complete strokes (two mechanical cycles)": it means four strokes = two crankshaft revolutions; hence four-stroke power = W_cycle·N/2.

Slide Ch.2 p.3 is an animated GIF of a cut-away turbojet: only one frame is readable. Slide Ch.2 pages whose image was NOT viewed: 1–9, 11, 12, 14, 17, 19–22, 26, 28, 29, 32–35, 37, 41–43, 47, 49–51, 53–56 (they rest on the sampled-checked OCR text); the pages whose formulas or numbers I use were viewed: 25, 31, 40, 44, 45, 48, 52 (and the earlier QA viewed 10, 13, 15, 16, 18, 23, 24, 27, 30, 36, 38, 39, 46).

Tutorials I #1 (pp.1–6): the statement says 17 °C but the solution takes T₁ = 290 K (290.15 K changes T₃ by +0.3 K only); R = 0.287 is not printed; v₁ = 0.832 is rounded (MEP 574 versus 574.2 computed exactly). T₂, T₃, T₄ come from linear interpolation of Table A-17.

Tutorials I #2 (pp.7–13): the slide says the constant specific heats are "at 25 °C/77 °F" but the solution uses 80 °F (540 R); it cites "Table A–2a" (the English-unit table is A-2E(a)); temperatures and pressures use k = 1.4 but the heats use c_p = 0.240 and c_v = 0.171 (ratio 1.4035), so η = 0.632 versus 0.6316 from the exact k = 1.4 formula; the MEP "110 psia" is rounded from 109.5.

Tutorials I #3 (p.14, = Cengel 9–37): neither c_v nor R is printed (default A-2a: 0.718; 0.287); 35 °C is 308 or 308.15 K (P₃ 6072 or 6069 kPa; MEP 0.08 %); T₄ = 800 K is the end of expansion and fixes T₃ (it is not redundant). Printed answers: 1969 K; 6072 kPa; 0.59 kJ; 59.4 %; 652 kPa: they match.

Tutorials I #4 (p.15): no table is named (A-17E used because the temperatures are in R) and P₁ is not given so the MEP cannot be computed (it is not asked); "(c) Carnot" uses absolute temperatures in R (1 − 540/2400 = 0.775).

Tutorials I #5 (p.16, = Cengel 9–47): no table named (A-17 used); 27 °C = 300 K. Printed answers 1724.8 K; 56.3 %; 675.9 kPa; linear interpolation gives 1724.7 K; 56.3 %; 675.6 kPa (rounding differences).
Tutorials I #6 (p.17, = Cengel 9–51): c_p, c_v, R, k are not printed (A-2a used: 1.005; 0.718; 0.287; 1.4); 20 °C = 293 K; r_c is not given but follows from T_max.
Tutorials I #7 (p.28): no table named (A-17E used); no solution on the slide: T₂ = 996.5 R; r_bw = 0.485; η = 0.465.

Tutorials I #8 (p.29): the statement does not say P₃ = P₂ (no combustor loss) nor the turbine exhaust pressure (taken as 100 kPa = P₁); T₂ = 580 K is the ACTUAL compressor state (implied isentropic efficiency ≈ 0.78 at r_p = 7), not an isentropic one. Results: T₃ = 1417 K; w_turb = 542.0; w_comp = 285.9 kJ/kg; ratio 0.527; η = 0.270.

Tutorials I Brayton example (pp.18–23, = Cengel 9–5): the slide rounds T₂ to 540 K and takes h₂ = 544.35 (the 540 K row); P_r2 = 11.09 actually corresponds to 539.86 K, h₂ = 544.18; consequently r_bw = 0.403 (slide) versus 0.4022 (exact). Slide p.23 prints only q_out, not the final η (p.22 prints 0.426).

Cengel 9–59 (page image of p.541 viewed): the statement prints an air–fuel ratio of 24, but the printed answers (2383 K; r_c = 2.7; 4.36 kJ; 0.543; 969 kPa; 72.7 kW; 159 g/kWh) are reproduced only with a ratio of 25 (verify_m02.py: AF = 25 gives 2383 K, 4.36 kJ, 969 kPa, 72.7 kW, 159 g/kWh; AF = 24 gives 2445 K, r_c = 2.77, MEP 1004 kPa). The site answers the printed statement (24) and shows both.

Cengel 9–96 and 9–119: the statements name no specific-heat assumption, but the printed answers (783 K; 108.1 kJ/kg; 22.5 % and 9089 N) match only Table A-17 (constant c_p = 1.005 gives 748 K; 95.3 kJ/kg; 21.2 % and 9318 N). The site's questions say "use A-17".
Cengel 9–16 (printed 3360 K) versus 3365 K computed from T₂ = 579.2 K and c_p = 1.005: 0.15 % off, three-significant-figure rounding; η = 21.0 % matches.

El-Sayed Example 4.2 (pp.216–218): the printed solution has two arithmetic slips: T₀₃ = 287.8·2.035 = 585.7 K (the book prints 587.5 K and uses it for T₀₅ = 1106.1 K) and T₇ = 1106.1/1.9283 = 573.6 K (the book prints 563.6 K). Hence the printed V_j = 1044.34 m/s, ṁ_a = 16.06 kg/s, η_p = 45.97 %, η_th = 60.36 %, η_o = 27.75 % are NOT right; recomputed V_j = 1036.2 m/s, ṁ_a = 16.2 kg/s, η_th = 0.591, η_o = 0.273. The printed answers are not used as the correct answers; only f = 0.0198 and T₀₂ = 287.8 K agree.

Dropped (reason): Cengel §9-7 Stirling/Ericsson (no slide); §9-12 second-law analysis and 9–122/9–123 (outside the slides); the dual cycle (no slide) and 9–130; 9–136 (T₃ = 2100 K lies outside the 273–1800 K validity range of the A-2c polynomial so route B cannot be used); 9–23 is kept but uses only P_r; problems needing T–s charts; the R-134a refrigeration example of Tutorials I pp.24–27 belongs to m03.
